game.name: Shotgun King: The Final Checkmate
game.short_description: Chess, but you replace your entire army with a royal shotgun. A unique strategy roguelike based on the timeless checkboard classic.

placements.verbal_evidence: "I'll put it as a scene" (ASR for "a C"), after "it was fun when I played it" and "pretty small game"

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Shotgun King is a chess roguelike where you play only the king, armed with a shotgun, clearing boards of white pieces. Each new board grants abilities that usually come with a downside while enemies also get stronger. He respects the unique, funny, low-seriousness concept and calls it a chill, simple game good for casual play such as on a Steam Deck. His main complaint is that the board never changes, so it gets boring, and that there is one boss and only minor unlock variety. He places it in C tier (ASR 'a scene').
praise: Unique, funny concept: chess merged with a roguelike and a shotgun
Per-board abilities change how each run plays despite the same board
Upgrades paired with downsides while enemies scale up, which keeps it interesting
Chill, simple and casual, well suited to Steam Deck play
criticism: The chess board never changes, which becomes boring and tiring over time
He thinks the board itself should have been altered, since the roguelike already rewrites the chess rules
Only a single boss, so the run ends abruptly
Unlocks are minor: new guns are not very different from each other, giving weak meta-variety
Small game he is unlikely to return to
unique_points: Chess rules turned into roguelike systems with extra caveats and rules
Playing as the king with a shotgun inverts the usual chess dynamic
Design lesson: if a roguelike rewrites the rules, it should consider varying the arena too
commentary.quote: it was fun when I played it
comparisons: other roguelikes with more varied starting customization
design_criteria: Level/arena variety: fixed chess board becomes repetitive
Risk vs reward: abilities come with downsides as enemies get stronger
Meta-progression: gun unlocks are too similar to matter much
Run structure: single boss, short simple runs
Replayability: per-run abilities vary but the board does not

community.one_liner: A turn-based chess-roguelike where you play a lone black king with a shotgun against a full white army, picking paired buff/debuff cards after each stage.
community.consensus_summary: Shotgun King is a well-liked indie: Steam shows about 91% positive across roughly 7,450 reviews (Very Positive), and the store page lists 93% overall at the time of fetch. Players praise the absurd-but-working premise, the card system and the short, replayable runs. Critics are fewer and more lukewarm: Metacritic's PS5 page shows 75 from 5 reviews (Wikipedia lists Switch at 82 from 4), with criticism aimed at difficulty spikes and limited replay value. Metacritic users are noticeably harsher (6.6 from 25 ratings) than Steam players, mostly over RNG-driven card pools and balance. It is not early access; it launched May 2022, got console ports in Aug 2023, and was still being patched through 2025 with the 1.6 Bad Company update and later 1.62x fixes.
best_things: High-concept premise (chess king with a shotgun) that keeps chess's planning and tactics while feeling fresh and funny
Buff/debuff card system: each stage you choose one white card (enemy buff) and one black card (your buff), which keeps runs different and builds interesting
Strong card interactions and synergies, with many builds on both sides of the board and some combos rewarded with achievements
Short runs (about 20 minutes) and a low price (around $10), so it is easy to pick up; a demo exists
Accessible to chess novices and often described as more fun than regular chess because of the roguelike variety
Fitting retro pixel art, sound design and music
Lots of content and life: 20 difficulty ranks, endless mode, Chase and Charnier modes, 100+ achievements, Workshop/mod support, free updates
Developer returned with a large free update years after launch (v1.6, about 30 new cards, 2 shotguns, 5 ranks), which players welcomed
worst_things: Heavy RNG in card offers; at high ranks the draws can be anti-player and runs feel decided before you can build anything
Enemy scaling outpaces the player: enemy health and buffs stack while shotgun damage barely grows, so late ranks feel unfair
Discovered checks and self-inflicted deaths from firing and opening a line are instant losses and feel cheap, even with blunder shields that only cover some cases
Card pool bloat: prerequisite cards and large pools make it rare to find synergies you want
No mid-run saving in a roguelike, which players find painful for long high-rank runs
Some cards and unlock paths are weak or hidden, and several shotgun unlocks are very hard to earn
Achievement hunting relies on luck and specific multi-card combos, not skill (a recurring complaint from 100%-ers)
Some mechanic interactions are undocumented and must be discovered by trial and error
improvements: Restore or add a proper toggle that highlights dangerous/check tiles (the middle-mouse highlight was removed in an update and moved behind a cheat/mod, which players see as an accessibility loss)
Give players more control over draws: card banishing, more rerolls, or smarter offers so the pool does not bloat
Rebalance late ranks and some cards/units so player scaling keeps pace with enemy scaling
Improve progression and unlocks (especially alternate shotguns) and make achievements less luck-dependent
Better in-game explanation of card interactions and warnings for discovered attacks; fix controller/Steam Deck issues such as grenades
unique_things: You are a single king with a shotgun versus a full chess army, so the chess rules stay intact but your only weapon is the shotgun
Dual card picks that simultaneously buff you and empower the enemy army, so difficulty is part of the build rather than a separate slider
Reviewers and players describe it as playing like a turn-based tactics game as much as chess: managing ammo, spread and damage matters more than chess openings
Shotgun mechanics on a chessboard: firing pushes you back, killing pieces can expose your king, and the AI sets traps with queens, bishops behind pawns, etc.
Steam Workshop and Lua modding support plus many modes (endless, Chase, Charnier raiding mode)
tedious_or_disliked: Repetitive loop: commentary from critics and Metacritic users is that you see most of the game's content within the first ~20 rounds
Slow, stressful board-scanning at high ranks when you can no longer easily see which tiles are dangerous
Hitting a hard wall around rank 7-9 or 10+ where losses feel RNG-driven rather than earned
Achievement and codex grinding that depends on drawing specific card combos
Losing a long run with no save to a single misclick or discovered check
divisive_points: Is the difficulty fair? Many Steam players say losses feel deserved and skill-based, while others say late ranks are pure luck
Replayability: Steam players praise it as highly replayable, while critics (PLAY, Push Square) and Metacritic users call it repetitive
Update direction: the 1.6 content update was celebrated, but the removal of the check-tile highlight and a censored tutorial line drew negative reviews from some longtime players
Whether it is really chess: some say it becomes a turn-based shooter rather than a chess game
community.reception_notes: Launched on PC May 12, 2022 to very strong Steam reception; PC Gamer is quoted on the store page calling it a supremely addictive turn-based roguelike. Console ports (Switch, PS4/5, Xbox) followed Aug 24, 2023, with physical Switch/PS5 editions shipping Apr 25, 2025 after delays (per Wikipedia). The v1.6 Bad Company update (April, anniversary update) added roughly 30 cards, a Charnier raiding mode, 2 shotguns, 5 ranks and 10 achievements; v1.62x patches through summer fixed softlocks, AI bugs, Steam Deck and macOS control issues. Some recent negative Steam reviews cite the removed check-tile highlight, card-pool bloat and a censored tutorial line. Steam lists no Metacritic score (the PC version is not scored); Metacritic only has console scores. Steam-revenue-calculator estimates about $1.89M gross and about $556k net; SteamSpy owner estimate 200k-500k (order-of-magnitude only). Publisher is listed as PUNKCAKE Delicieux on Steam and Headbang Club on Wikipedia. OpenCritic page could not be located; WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the score is null.
